title: Shore blocking turns one descending sequence below an ordinal into one below its natural product
source_title: Conservation of Ramsey's theorem for pairs and well-foundedness

standard_prerequisites.name: Natural sum and natural product of ordinals below epsilon_0
standard_prerequisites.statement: For ordinals alpha and beta below epsilon_0 written with a common family of exponents, the natural sum is obtained by adding the coefficients of like powers of omega, and alpha ntimes k is the natural sum of alpha with itself k times; the article's own definition is retained at source lines 392-398.
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the two operations that the counted lemma uses in both its hypothesis and its conclusion, namely beta below alpha and the larger ordinal beta ntimes k.

standard_prerequisites.name: Theories RCA_0, I Sigma_1 and the well-foundedness statement WF(alpha)
standard_prerequisites.statement: RCA_0 is the standard base theory of reverse mathematics; I Sigma_1 is the induction scheme for Sigma^0_1 formulas; WF(alpha) states that the ordinal alpha is well founded, and a model M satisfies WF(alpha) when it has no M-infinite descending sequence of ordinals below alpha; these are the standard notions of the reverse-mathematics literature and the article uses the notations RCA_0, I Sigma_1 and WF(alpha) throughout, for example in its abstract and introduction.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is stated for a model M of RCA_0 plus WF(alpha) and its proof invokes I Sigma_1 to make the constructed Turing functional total, so both theories and the meaning of the well-foundedness statement must be available.

standard_prerequisites.name: M[X] and the forcing extension by a real
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a model M = (M,S) of second-order arithmetic and a real X in 2^M, the article writes M[X] for the extension of M by the real X; the counted lemma is stated for every X with M[X] a model of RCA_0.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypothesis and the proof both quantify over reals X such that the extension M[X] satisfies RCA_0, and the proof appeals to M[X] satisfying I Sigma_1.

core_obligations: Normalise the Turing functionals by a twisting argument so that whenever Phi^sigma_e(n) converges one has n below the length of sigma, convergence of Phi^sigma_e(m) for every m below n, and the values Phi^sigma_e(0), ..., Phi^sigma_e(n) form a strictly decreasing sequence of ordinals below beta (source lines 434-439).

For sigma in 2^{<M} and e below k define alpha(sigma,e) as the value Phi^sigma_e(s) at the largest s below the length of sigma where it converges, and set alpha(sigma,e) = beta when there is no such s; note that alpha(sigma',e) is at most alpha(sigma,e) whenever sigma' extends sigma (source line 441).

Build the functional Gamma_k by a search over extensions: on input n it looks for x above the length of sigma_{n-1} and sigma_n compatible with X such that Phi^{sigma_n}_e(x) converges for some e below k, and if it finds them it outputs the natural sum alpha(sigma,0) nplus ... nplus alpha(sigma,k-1); then Gamma^X_k(n), when defined, is an ordinal below beta ntimes k (source lines 443-444).
Assume X is such that M[X] satisfies RCA_0 and that some Phi^X_e with e below k is total; use that M[X] satisfies I Sigma_1 to conclude that Gamma^X is total (source lines 446-447).

Verify strict decrease: because x is above the length of sigma_{n-1}, and by item (1) Phi^{sigma_{n-1}}_e(x) diverges for the e that converges on sigma_n, items (2) and (3) give alpha(sigma_{n+1},e) strictly below alpha(sigma_n,e), hence Gamma^X_k(n+1) is strictly below Gamma^X_k(n) (source line 449).

Conclude that Gamma^X_k is an M-infinite strictly decreasing sequence of ordinals below beta ntimes k, and that an index for Gamma_k is computable in k, since the search uses only k and beta (source lines 428-430 and 449).

proof_roadmap.step: Twist the functionals so that convergence on an input forces convergence and strict decrease on all smaller inputs.
Define alpha(sigma,e) and record its monotonicity in sigma.
Define the functional Gamma_k by an increasing search and note that its outputs are natural sums below beta ntimes k.
Use totality of some Phi^X_e together with I Sigma_1 of M[X] to show Gamma^X is total.
Show the outputs strictly decrease and conclude.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2402.11616v3 的 Lemma lem:shore-blocking-wf（源 426-431 行，证明 433-450 行，共 18 行）：在模型 M 中，若存在某个 e<k 使 Phi^X_e 是小于 beta 的 M-无穷下降序列，则存在一个可由 k 计算指标的 Turing 泛函 Gamma_k，使 Gamma^X_k 是小于 beta ⨯ k（自然积）的 M-无穷下降序列。关键操作不是例行核验：作者必须先把泛函「扭」成收敛即蕴含对更小输入也收敛、且输出构成严格下降序列的形式（434-439 行），再定义 alpha(sigma,e) 为其最后收敛值并证明它对 sigma 单调（441 行），然后用「寻找更长的相容扩展」的搜索构造 Gamma_k，使其输出恰为 k 个 alpha 的自然和，从而落在 beta ⨯ k 之下（443-444 行）；totality 靠 M[X] 满足 I Sigma_1（447 行），严格下降靠第 (1)(2)(3) 条的配合（449 行）。难点在于把「存在一条下降序列」通过 Shore blocking 同时满足到 M 的越来越长的初始段上，并让指标随 k 可计算；原文位置在证明的 434-444 行与 446-449 行。
